llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions match a RAGFlow dataset client, but the registry metadata does not declare the required API credential or base-URL configuration and the scripts will send local files and JSON to whatever base URL is provided — these mismatches and the open-ended base_url are concerning and should be clarified before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description say it's a RAGFlow dataset manager and the bundled scripts implement dataset/document/list/upload/parse/model-listing operations — that is coherent. However the skill metadata (registry requirements) declares no required environment variables or primary credential, while SKILL.md and the scripts clearly require a RAGFLOW_API_KEY and a RAGFlow base URL at runtime. The missing declaration in the registry is an incoherence that matters for permission/credential gating.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md restricts the agent to run only the bundled scripts, and the scripts' behavior matches the stated scope (list/create/delete datasets, upload docs, start/stop parse, check status, search, list models). The scripts do read local files (for uploads and for @path JSON options like parser-config or --data) and will POST file contents and JSON to the provided base_url. That file I/O and network I/O are expected for this purpose, but SKILL.md does not constrain or validate the base_url (it relies on the runtime-provided URL), so a malicious or incorrect base_url could be used for exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), so nothing is downloaded or executed during install beyond the included scripts. The skill ships Python scripts but does not pull external code during installation; this lowers install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime clearly expects a RAGFLOW_API_KEY and a base URL (the SKILL.md explicitly states this and the scripts call require_api_key/resolve_base_url). Yet the registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential. That omission is disproportionate and misleading. Also the scripts allow reading arbitrary local files (via upload paths and @path JSON flags) which will be transmitted to the configured base URL — the skill legitimately needs file access for uploads, but that increases the impact of an attacker-controllable base_url.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced always-on (always: false) and does not request to modify other skills or system configurations. Autonomous invocation is enabled (the platform default), which is expected for skills; no extra persistence or elevated privilege is requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package implements a RAGFlow HTTP client and will read local files and send content to whatever base URL and API key are provided at runtime. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Ask the publisher/registry owner to declare the required environment variables (RAGFLOW_API_KEY and the base URL) and set the primary credential so permission gates can apply. 2) Only provide a base URL you trust (the official RAGFlow endpoint); do not allow an unfamiliar or attacker-controlled domain, otherwise uploaded files and JSON could be exfiltrated. 3) Be aware the scripts can read local @path JSON files (parser-config, meta-fields, --data) and will upload files you pass; avoid uploading sensitive files unless you trust the endpoint. 4) Verify the delete/parse guardrails in SKILL.md are enforced in practice (the SKILL.md asks for explicit IDs/confirmation). If you cannot get the required metadata corrected or cannot confirm the official base URL, treat the skill as risky and do not install.
